subject: ss-neurology
title: Acute Reperfusion Therapy and Mechanical Thrombectomy

steps.tx: Intravenous thrombolysis remains the primary medical reperfusion strategy in eligible patients presenting with **acute ischaemic stroke** within **4.5 hours** of symptom onset. Standard therapeutic regimens include intravenous **alteplase 0.9 mg/kg** with a maximum ceiling of 90 mg or intravenous **tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg** administered as a rapid single bolus with a maximum of 25 mg. Tenecteplase offers significant pharmacological advantages including higher fibrin specificity, longer half-life, and superior rates of early arterial recanalization prior to endovascular intervention.
steps.say: Intravenous thrombolysis serves as the cornerstone of medical reperfusion for acute ischaemic stroke within four point five hours of onset. Prescribed regimens include tenecteplase zero point two five milligrams per kilogram bolus or alteplase zero point nine milligrams per kilogram infusion. Tenecteplase provides distinct operational advantages with rapid single bolus delivery and superior early arterial recanalization rates.

steps.tx: Strict blood pressure control is mandatory before initiating intravenous thrombolytic infusion. Prior to starting **thrombolysis**, arterial blood pressure must be reduced to a **systolic below 185 mmHg** and a **diastolic below 110 mmHg**. Preferred first-line intravenous antihypertensive agents include intravenous **labetalol** boluses, continuous intravenous nicardipine infusion, or clevidipine titration. Rapid uncontrolled pressure swings must be prevented during acute therapy to safeguard marginal cerebral perfusion while preventing vascular rupture.
steps.say: Strict hemodynamic targets must be secured before administering intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischaemic stroke. Systolic blood pressure must fall below one hundred eighty five millimeters of mercury and diastolic below one hundred ten millimeters of mercury. Intravenous labetalol boluses or continuous nicardipine infusions are the preferred first line options to achieve safe blood pressure levels.

steps.tx: Following reperfusion therapy, intensive hemodynamic monitoring is essential to prevent hemorrhagic complications. For the initial **24 hours** after intravenous thrombolysis or endovascular intervention, arterial blood pressure must be strictly maintained below **180/105 mmHg**. Sustained pressures exceeding this ceiling exponentially heighten the danger of symptomatic **intracerebral haemorrhage** within reperfused capillary beds. Neurological vital signs and automated cuff blood pressure recordings are documented every 15 minutes during the initial two hours of therapy.
steps.say: Following reperfusion therapy, arterial blood pressure must remain strictly below one hundred eighty over one hundred five millimeters of mercury for twenty four hours. Maintaining blood pressure below this threshold prevents symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage into friable reperfused parenchyma. Frequent neurological evaluations and scheduled blood pressure measurements are vital throughout this high risk interval.

steps.tx: Pre-procedural parenchymal evaluation relies on non-contrast cranial computed tomography scored by **ASPECTS** criteria. The **ASPECTS** rating system systematically examines **10** distinct anatomic zones in the middle cerebral artery territory, deducting one point for each region displaying early parenchymal hypoattenuation. Baseline scores **under 6** denote extensive irreversible **infarction** of the ischemic core. Conversely, scores of 6 to 10 confirm preserved tissue viability suitable for emergency revascularization.
steps.say: The Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score evaluates ten predetermined anatomic regions across the middle cerebral artery territory on non contrast scans. Each territory displaying ischemic hypoattenuation loses one point from baseline. Scores under six designate extensive irreversible ischemic core infarction, whereas scores of six or higher reflect favourable parenchymal preservation.

Corona radiata, M4, M5, M6 cortical territories
Scores under 6 reflect extensive established core
Maximum 10 points on baseline non-contrast CT
Score 6 to 10 predicts favourable functional recovery

steps.tx: Emergency **mechanical thrombectomy** represents the standard of care within **6** hours of symptom onset for patients with large vessel occlusion involving the intracranial internal carotid artery or proximal middle cerebral artery M1 segment. Candidates must present with an initial **ASPECTS** score of **6** or greater alongside functional independence prior to stroke onset. Urgent groin puncture and rapid intracranial catheter navigation directly restore microvascular perfusion and dramatically decrease long-term neurological disability.
steps.say: Emergency mechanical thrombectomy provides proven standard of care within six hours of onset for patients with large vessel occlusion. Eligible candidates present with internal carotid or proximal middle cerebral artery occlusion and an ASPECTS score of six or greater. Prompt endovascular retrieval of the occlusive thrombus provides substantial reductions in long term functional disability.

steps.tx: The therapeutic window for **thrombectomy** extends successfully up to **24** hours from last known well in select patients demonstrating salvageable tissue. Large multicentre randomized investigations including the DAWN and **DEFUSE-3** trials validated advanced automated perfusion mismatch criteria. Patients presenting between 6 and 24 hours qualify when neuroimaging demonstrates a small established ischemic core coupled with a substantially larger volume of critically hypoperfused but viable ischemic penumbra.
steps.say: The treatment window for endovascular thrombectomy extends up to twenty four hours in selected patients based on advanced perfusion neuroimaging. Landmark trials including DAWN and DEFUSE three established clinical and automated volumetric mismatch criteria. Demonstrating a small ischemic core surrounded by an extensive hypoperfused penumbra reliably predicts significant functional benefit from late recanalization.

rows: Clinical deficit disproportionate to infarct volume on MRI or CT
Small ischemic core (<70 ml) and penumbra mismatch ratio >= 1.8

steps.tx: Technical success during catheter-based revascularization is evaluated using the modified Treatment in Cerebral Ischemia scale. The **mTICI** classification grades angiographic perfusion following clot extraction, with grade 0 indicating no flow and grade 3 indicating complete normal distal vessel filling. Achieving an **mTICI** grade of **2b** or 3 defines successful angiographic **recanalization**, which correlates directly with clinical recovery, decreased mortality, and reduced cerebral edema.
steps.say: Angiographic reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy is graded using the modified Treatment in Cerebral Ischemia scale. Grades range from zero representing absence of forward flow to three representing complete distal parenchymal reperfusion. Reaching a grade of two b or three establishes successful recanalization and serves as the primary technical benchmark of procedural success.

steps.tx: Post-thrombolytic pharmacology demands rigorous antiplatelet restriction to avoid life-threatening parenchymal hemorrhage. Oral antiplatelet agents including oral **aspirin** must be strictly withheld for **24** hours following intravenous **alteplase** or tenecteplase administration. Follow-up non-contrast cranial computed tomography performed at 24 hours must definitively exclude petechial hemorrhagic transformation or hematoma before initiating maintenance antiplatelet or anticoagulant regimens.
steps.say: All antiplatelet agents including aspirin must be completely withheld for twenty four hours after administering intravenous alteplase or tenecteplase. A mandatory non contrast cranial computed tomography scan at twenty four hours must confirm the absence of intracranial hemorrhage before commencing antiplatelet therapy. This scheduled imaging pause ensures maximal patient safety following thrombolytic reperfusion.
